name: i-have-adhd
works_with: Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, OpenCode, Pi, Grok and more
short: Makes your coding agent lead with the next action, number its steps and drop the filler.
what: A skill with 10 output rules for your coding agent. It leads with the next action, numbers multi-step tasks, ends with one concrete next step, skips tangents, caps lists at five items and drops preambles and closers. No ADHD diagnosis needed.
who: Anyone who's tired of scrolling past "Great question!" to find the command. It still explains fully when you ask it to explain.
needs: A supported coding agent. INSTALL.md has steps for more than a dozen

steps.title: Claude Code
steps.code:
claude plugin marketplace add ayghri/i-have-adhd
claude plugin install i-have-adhd@i-have-adhd

steps.title: Codex
steps.text: Codex won't switch it on by itself. Type `$i-have-adhd` to use it.
steps.code:
codex plugin marketplace add ayghri/i-have-adhd --ref main
codex plugin add i-have-adhd@i-have-adhd

steps.title: Gemini CLI (always on)
steps.text: The extension applies the rules from the first message. `git` must be installed.

steps.title: Cursor, Copilot and other skills-compatible agents
Optional: always on in Claude Code
steps.text: A start-of-session hook loads the rules when this flag file exists. Delete the file to go back to on-demand.

try.label: From the README
try.text:
/i-have-adhd

Then ask your usual question. Say "stop adhd mode" or "normal mode" to turn it off for the session.

watch: The README's first install option is a prompt you paste into your agent so it installs itself by reading the repo's AGENTS.md. We listed the manual commands from INSTALL.md instead, so you can see what runs.
In Claude Code, Codex, Qwen Code and Grok nothing changes until you invoke it. Other agents may switch it on by themselves.
On Grok the install needs `--trust`, which lets the plugin's hooks and skills run.
